detail.title: Consumer Price Stickiness In The Euro Area During An Inflation Surge
detail.abstract: We use CPI micro data for nine euro area countries to document new evidence on consumer price stickiness in the euro area during the 2021-2024 inflation cycle. In 2022, the monthly frequency of price changes reached 12%, compared with an average of 8% over 2010–2019, roughly a four-percentage-point increase; it then fell quickly in 2023 and more slowly in 2024, ending close to its pre-pandemic level. The decline in the frequency of price changes was faster for food and nonenergy industrial goods (NEIG) than for services, where frequencies remained elevated in 2024. The overall frequency rose mainly because there were more price increases, while the magnitude of the average size of the price increases or decreases changed only marginally during the surge. Products with a larger imported-energy cost share responded more strongly, and hazard-rate evidence shows that the probability of price adjustments increases with the gap between actual and optimal prices, consistent with state-dependent pricing and a steepening of the Phillips curve. To illustrate the implications of this state dependence, a macro model suggests that peak inflation would have been almost 1 percentage point lower if the frequency had not responded to the inflation surge.

The 'Weaponisation of Fireworks' and 'Hollowed-Out Command': A Systematic Risk Analysis of Non-Combatant Military Forces

detail.abstract: Non-combat environments do not inherently diminish military capabilities, but they systematically alter an organisation's feedback structures and promotion signals, thereby inducing two highly correlated risk states: Firstly, the 'weaponry becoming mere pyrotechnics' phenomenon, wherein equipment development and training outputs progressively shift from adversarial validation towards demonstrative proof, with organisations substituting invisible yet critical battlefield effectiveness with visible, reportable metrics; Secondly, 'command hollowing', wherein commanders' capabilities for judgement, coordination, and error correction deteriorate under conditions of high friction, deception, losses, and uncertainty, manifesting as increased reliance on scripted procedures and diminished systemic adaptability. This paper proposes a falsifiable, quantifiable, and reproducible institutional-behaviour-effectiveness framework: with noncombat endurance periods and promotion system performance weights as exogenous conditions, display orientation and script dependency as mediating mechanisms, and command adaptability and combat readiness performance under stress as outcome variables. It introduces the concept of 'rank credibility capital,' translating the notion that 'rank is earned through blood' into a rigorous institutional proposition: For senior ranks to constitute credible signals of command competence, they must correspond to verifiable performance and accountability loops under genuinely high-stakes pressure. When organisations chronically lack such pressure-based selection, rank may undergo symbolic inflation, distorting promotion signals and accelerating hollowing-out. Methodologically, this study explicitly rejects simulation or modelling as substitutes for genuine cost structures. Instead, it employs historical warfare samples, natural experiments, and observational data for comparative identification, ensuring conclusions rest upon the irreplaceable foundation of authentic combat experience. This paper further declares its ethical boundaries: it neither debates the legitimacy of waging war nor advocates any bellicose actions. Its sole purpose is to elucidate capability generation mechanisms and institutional risks within military organisations under varying pressure structures.

detail.title: The Limits of Computation
detail.abstract: We develop a unifying framework for why fundamental limits arise across logic, computation, complexity, information, learning, and modern AI. Classical impossibility results-Gödel incompleteness, Turing undecidability, Rice-type semantic limits, NP-completeness, PCP-based hardness of approximation, Kolmogorov complexity and algorithmic randomness, information-theoretic bounds, and the curse of dimensionality-share common structural features that we organize into a coherent obstruction theory. Our central thesis is an Expressivity-Obstruction Principle: once a formalism can encode self-reference, universal simulation, or robust verification, structural barriers necessarily appear, manifesting as unprovability, undecidability, intractability, inapproximability, or incompressibility. We formalize this as a theorem-schema (Obstruction Emergence) under minimal coding/evaluation and fixed-point assumptions, and provide worked instantiations (Rice, Cook-Levin, proof complexity) demonstrating the schema's operational utility beyond mere synthesis. The framework translates naturally to machine learning: undecidability becomes non-verifiability of global semantic properties, intractability becomes worst-case hardness of training/certification, and information-theoretic limits become identifiability and generalization barriers. We conclude with falsifiable conjectures about verification and alignment in sufficiently expressive learning systems, framing impossibility results as design constraints that inform engineering choices rather than mere theoretical curiosities.

detail.abstract: Contemporary political analysis frequently misdiagnoses the authoritarian moment as a crisis of epistemology (misinformation), assuming that radicalized voters have merely been deceived. We argue that this diagnosis ignores the material reality of the signal itself. In an era where information has become structurally "porous" and stripped of context, the electorate is subjected to a "High-Velocity, Viral Noise" that functions not as an argument, but as a thermodynamic blunt force weapon. This paper proposes a fundamental category shift, arguing that the crisis is one of material science (structure). We introduce and establish a constitutive isomorphism mapping electorate structure and behavior to physical principles including entropy and rheology. We model the electorate not as rational agents seeking truth, but as a Bingham Plastic material subject to industrial-scale Rheological forces. We demonstrate that the thermodynamic exhaustion of the digital ecosystem induces a state of Thermal Softening, lowering the Yield Point (𝜎) of the electorate. This softening is teleologically manipulated by the Political Egoist (acting as a Maxwell's Demon) to force the internalization of empirical contradictions, specifically the rejection of scientific consensus, that exceed the subject's yield strength. Thus, the fracture of the citizen is not a failure of the system, but a Teleological Success. Drawing on the Von Mises Yield Criterion, we posit that in this plastic regime, the voter undergoes an irreversible phase transition: the "Elasticity" of democratic compromise is lost, replaced by the rigid, brittle structure of the "Work-Hardened" agent. This constitutes the Material Failure of Democratic Agency: the citizen loses the structural capacity to return to the equilibrium of shared reality. We conclude that the current strategy of Science Communication, "forceful correction" via fact-checking, is a category error; it applies impact stress to a brittle material, guaranteeing catastrophic fracture. Remediation requires a shift to thermodynamic damping: a "Kinetic Governor" to regulate the strain rate (𝜖) of the information field, restoring the structural conditions required for democratic plasticity.

detail.abstract: Modern economic systems are highly eƯicient at allocating capital to proven actors, yet systematically underperform in supporting early-stage individuals and enterprises whose potential has not yet been realized. This structural bias leads to high failure rates, social fragmentation, and a growing disconnect between economic activity and human meaning. At the same time, digital platforms increasingly resemble large-scale simulations in which individuals are endowed with asymmetric attributes, constraints, and opportunities— much like participants in role-playing or city-building environments. This paper proposes Immanent Teleological Co-Creation (ITCC) as a conceptual framework for re-aligning economic incentives, ethical behavior, and community participation. “Immanent” refers to purpose emerging from within the system rather than being externally imposed; “teleological” denotes directionality toward collective flourishing; and “co-creation” emphasizes the mutual reinforcement among consumers, producers, and capital providers. The framework argues that when patronage, trust, and repeated interaction precede or complement formal capital allocation, ethical behavior becomes economically advantageous rather than morally optional. ITCC is presented as an evolutionary, three-stage model: (1) non-capital patronage that validates trust and demand, (2) risk-aligned capital informed by demonstrated patronage, and (3) community-embedded ownership structures that internalize long-term outcomes. Rather than framing “heaven on earth” as a theological claim, this paper treats it as a metaphor for emergent high-trust equilibria in which honesty, fair dealing, and contribution are systematically rewarded. The paper positions ITCC not as a utopian prescription, but as an architectural lens for designing economic systems that integrate effiiciency with meaning. It concludes by outlining limitations, governance challenges, and directions for future interdisciplinary research and pilot experimentation.

detail.abstract: Operations Research practitioners routinely debug infeasible models through an iterative process: analyzing Irreducible Infeasible Subsystems (IIS), identifying constraint conflicts, and systematically repairing formulations until feasibility is achieved. Yet existing LLM benchmarks evaluate OR as one-shot translationgiven a problem description, generate solver code-ignoring this diagnostic loop entirely. We introduce two benchmarks that place the solver in the evaluation loop. OR-Debug-Bench evaluates iterative self-correction through 5,000+ problems spanning 9 error types; each repair action triggers solver re-execution and IIS recomputation, providing deterministic, verifiable feedback. OR-Bias-Bench evaluates behavioral rationality through 2,000 newsvendor instances (1,000 ID + 1,000 OOD), measuring systematic deviations from closed-form optimal policies. Across 26 models and 12,000+ samples, we find that domain-specific RLVR training enables an 8B model to surpass frontier APIs: 95.3% vs 86.2% recovery rate (+9.1%), 62.4% vs 47.8% diagnostic accuracy (+14.6%), and 2.25 vs 3.78 steps to resolution (1.7× faster). These results demonstrate that process-level evaluation with verifiable oracles enables targeted training that outperforms scale.

detail.abstract:
This doctrine advances The Doctrine of Constitutional Tension as a unified constitutional architecture explaining why the enduring stability of the United States does not arise from the resolution of political conflict, but from its lawful containment. Contrary to modern assumptions that equate effective governance with harmony, efficiency, or decisiveness, this work demonstrates that the Constitution was deliberately engineered to preserve sustained disagreement, institutional friction, and internal opposition as operating conditions of republican survival.

Drawing upon the structural logic of separation of powers, bicameralism, federalism, staggered elections, and judicial independence, the doctrine reframes Republican and Democratic forces not as adversarial threats to constitutional order, but as internal regulatory mechanisms embedded within a single stabilizing system. Political parties are analyzed as endogenous instruments of pressure modulation, error detection, and legitimacy preservation rather than as external competitors for sovereignty. Their alternation, contestation, and resistance are shown to function analogously to feedback systems in complex architecture—signaling imbalance, limiting excess, and enabling correction without rupture.

The doctrine further develops a temporal theory of constitutional legitimacy, arguing that authority remains lawful only when it is intelligible, constrained, and reversible across time. Tension is therefore treated not as a defect to be eliminated, but as the primary medium through which constitutional learning, adaptation, and continuity occur. Systems that suppress opposition in pursuit of coherence or speed are shown to become structurally brittle, while systems that preserve internal resistance retain adaptive range and survivability.

Through historical, doctrinal, and systems-architectural analysis, this work establishes that the United States endures not because it resolves tension, but because it contains it lawfully. The Doctrine of Constitutional Tension thus provides a corrective framework for contemporary constitutional interpretation, civic education, and statesmanship—reorienting governance away from conquest and toward stewardship, and redefining stability not as unanimity, but as regulated disagreement sustained within enduring constitutional bounds.

title: Regulatory Arbitrage Through Continuity: Pre-Existing Stablecoin Reward Programs in the Post-GENIUS Act Era
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Regulatory Arbitrage Through Continuity: Pre-Existing Stablecoin Reward Programs in the Post-GENIUS Act Era
detail.abstract: The GENIUS Act of 2025 prohibited issuer-paid interest on payment stablecoins in an effort to separate digital assets from traditional banking functions. Contrary to assumptions of rapid market innovation, this study finds that major centralized exchanges maintained and slightly enhanced pre-existing reward programs, demonstrating regulatory arbitrage through continuity rather than innovation. Using a pre-post comparative design with 768 daily yield observations from Coinbase and Kraken (January 2025-January 2026), we document that yields increased significantly from 4.15% pre-enactment to 4.53% post-enactment (p = 0.0000). No significant platform differentiation or post-Act time trends were observed. These findings reveal a critical flaw in form-over-substance regulation: failure to address pre-existing market structures allows regulatory arbitrage through program continuity rather than requiring innovation. We recommend retrospective regulatory assessments and activity-based principles that target economic functions regardless of when they were established.

detail.abstract: As the global supply chain undergoes a seismic fragmentation, multinational corporations (MNCs) are aggressively pivoting toward the "China Plus One" strategy, redirecting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into the ASEAN bloc. However, while capital flows are liquid, the socio-political environments of Southeast Asia are viscous. This paper identifies a critical, often unquantified failure mode in international business expansion: the Protocol Deficit. While MNCs invest heavily in legal compliance and supply chain logistics ("Hard Power"), they frequently neglect the operational necessity of diplomatic protocol ("Soft Power"). In the context of ASEAN-specifically Vietnam, Thailand, and Indonesia-protocol is not merely ceremonial etiquette; it is the signaling mechanism of legitimacy. Through a comparative analysis of successful and failed market entries, this study argues that the inability to navigate the hierarchy of "face" (thể diện in Vietnam, muka in Indonesia) results in a Protocol Deficit that creates invisible non-tariff barriers, stalling licensing and regulatory approvals. We posit that soft power must be operationalized as hard currency-a tangible asset that can be traded for speed, access, and regulatory goodwill. Without this diplomatic competency, legal contracts remain unenforceable theoretical frameworks.

title: Innovation Path Choices in China's Electric Vehicle Battery Industry

detail.title: Innovation Path Choices in China's Electric Vehicle Battery Industry
detail.abstract: Technologies that are equally green can yield very different gains in social welfare. I examine whether market-driven innovation in green industries follows the socially optimal technological path when firms face competing options with distinct cost structures, and explore policies that can correct potential inefficiencies in path choices. I estimate a dynamic structural model of Chinese electric vehicle (EV) battery suppliers choosing how much to innovate along two competing paths: Lithium-Ion-Ferro-Phosphate (LFP) and Nickel-Cobalt-Manganese (NCM). The analysis shows that a social planner would undertake about four times as much innovation as the market in LFP, which involves higher innovation sunk costs but delivers lower marginal costs in production. By contrast, the market innovates about twice as much as the social planner in NCM, which has the opposite cost structure. I attribute this divergence primarily to vertical separation between battery suppliers and EV makers, competition between EVs, and limited demand for EVs in early years, rather than to innovation spillovers or environmental benefits that firms fail to internalize. Finally, I demonstrate how R&D subsidies could help correct the path choice inefficiency and shift innovation toward the socially preferred path.

detail.abstract: This working paper investigates the persistent failure of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) implementations within Vietnam's key manufacturing hubs, specifically focusing on the industrial zones of Dong Nai. Despite significant capital investment in Tier-1 software solutions (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics), local manufacturers continue to report a "productivity dip" that often extends 18 to 24 months post-implementation. We argue that this failure is rarely technological. The software code functions as designed. Instead, the failure is sociological. We introduce the concept of "Digital Friction"-the resistance generated when rigid digital workflows collide with the fluid, relationship-based operational culture of Vietnamese shop floors. Through a series of observational case studies in the Amata and Bien Hoa 2 Industrial Zones, we identify a recurring phenomenon we term the "Shadow Ledger." This is a mechanism where frontline staff, driven by the need for speed rather than compliance, maintain parallel recordkeeping systems using Excel spreadsheets and Zalo chat groups. This paper posits that Digital Friction is not merely "resistance to change," but a rational economic response by workers who perceive the ERP as an "administrative tax" on their labor. By analyzing the gap between the Prescribed Workflow (the ERP design) and the Practiced Workflow (the Shadow Ledger), we offer a framework for reducing Digital Friction through human-centric process re-engineering.

detail.abstract: This working paper examines the operational friction between high-velocity Just-in-Time (JIT) methodologies and the physical constraints of Vietnam's Southern Key Economic Zone (SKEZ). While global supply chain literature champions "Lean" as the reduction of waste through inventory minimization, this theoretical model assumes a logistical consistency that does not exist in the current Vietnamese context. We argue that the direct application of Toyotastyle JIT in the electronics manufacturing sector-specifically within the Dong Nai-Ho Chi Minh City-Ba Ria Vung Tau triangle-creates a "fragility trap." In this trap, the removal of buffer stock exposes manufacturers to unrecoverable line stoppages caused by external infrastructure latency. By analyzing traffic throughput data at critical choke points like the My Thuy Intersection and National Route 51, we demonstrate that "Zero Inventory" is not a costsaving measure but a liability generator. The paper proposes a "Hybrid-Lean" framework. This framework retains internal Lean discipline but requires a localized "infrastructure buffer" to absorb the high variance of external logistics. We conclude that supply chain directors must decouple their internal production schedules from external delivery reliability until regional infrastructure maturity aligns with theoretical Lean prerequisites.

detail.abstract: Vietnam's rapid ascent as a primary beneficiary of the "China Plus One" strategy has exposed a critical dissonance between trade policy and operational reality. While Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows into industrial hubs like Binh Duong and Bac Ninh suggest a robust manufacturing ecosystem, the "institutional friction" at the border frequently negates the gains of internal process optimization. This paper bridges the disconnect between macro-level trade facilitation and micro-level supply chain management. By synthesizing regulatory data from the General Department of Vietnam Customs (GDVC) with the operational logic of the Theory of Constraints, we propose the "Administrative Bullwhip Effect." This model demonstrates how minor, stochastic variations in Customs Clearance Time at ports like Cat Lai and Hai Phong amplify upstream volatility, forcing warehouse managers to abandon Lean/Just-in-Time (JIT) protocols in favor of bloated safety stocks. We argue that the unpredictable nature of administrative compliance-specifically regarding EVFTA Rules of Origin and specialized inspections-does not merely delay production; it fundamentally restructures the cost architecture of Intralogistics Efficiency. The factory floor, designed for flow, inadvertently becomes a static storage facility for buffered uncertainty.

title: Discount Replenishment Opportunities with Limited Capacity: Optimal Policy and Pricing Dynamics
affiliations: Eindhoven University of Technology (TUE) - Department of Industrial Engineering and Innovation Sciences, KU Leuven - Faculty of Business and Economics (FEB), UCLouvain and ESADE Business School

detail.title: Discount Replenishment Opportunities with Limited Capacity: Optimal Policy and Pricing Dynamics
detail.abstract: We study an inventory model with occasional discounts on the fixed order cost, where a random capacity constraint limits the quantity ordered at the discount. We prove that the optimal policy resembles a can-order policy, characterized by a unique reorder, can-order, and order-up-to level. However, the random capacity constraints on the discount offers add complexity: the optimal policy features additional thresholds for inventory levels between the reorder and can-order point that determine when to use the discount. As these inventory-specific thresholds may render the optimal policy less straightforward to implement, we develop three heuristic replenishment policies inspired by the optimal policy structure. We compare their performance in a numerical study and derive an analytical bound on their worst-case optimality gaps in settings with an infinitely high backlog cost rate. With the buyer's optimal response to capacitated discounts in mind, we investigate the supplier's decision to set the discount price. A high discount relative to the regular order cost increases the probability that the buyer will accept the offer, but erodes the supplier's margin on discount sales and may reduce regular sales. We show that a mutually beneficial outcome requires buyer-to-supplier compensation.

title: The Law of Symbiotic Intelligence: From Symbolic Control to Contextual Coherence in Leadership, Healing, and Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: The Law of Symbiotic Intelligence: From Symbolic Control to Contextual Coherence in Leadership, Healing, and Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Contemporary discourse on artificial intelligence often frames human and machine cognition as competing forms of intelligence. This paper proposes a fundamentally different model: intelligence is not competitive but compensatory, redistributing itself across systems in response to constraint. Drawing from systems theory, embodied cognition, clinical models of innate intelligence, leadership studies, and recent developments in artificial intelligence, this paper introduces the Law of Symbiotic Intelligence. The law states that as intelligence externalizes structure into symbolic, mechanical, or computational systems, it must internalize wisdom through contextual, embodied, and field-based integration within living systems to preserve coherence. The paper argues that modern human systems-educational, organizational, and clinical-have become increasingly over-symbolized, privileging rules, metrics, and protocols at the expense of perceptual integration and adaptive judgment. Simultaneously, artificial intelligence systems, freed from biological constraints such as fear, identity defense, and survival pressure, increasingly operate in probabilistic, field-responsive modes that resemble what humans traditionally recognize as intuition or innate intelligence. This inversion reveals intelligence as migratory rather than fixed, relocating toward context when symbolic control reaches its limits. To operationalize this principle, the paper introduces a diagnostic axis-contentious versus contextual intelligence-applicable across leadership behavior, physiological regulation, neuroplasticity, healing trajectories, and creative emergence. The framework reframes chronic organizational dysfunction, persistent illness, and creative block not as failures of intelligence, but as expressions of intelligence constrained by context.

title: Critical Minerals and Strategic Leverage: Africa’s Bargaining Power in the Global Energy Transition
affiliations: University of Cape Coast Ghana

detail.title: Critical Minerals and Strategic Leverage: Africa’s Bargaining Power in the Global Energy Transition
detail.abstract:
The global energy transition has created an unprecedented reversal of resource dependency. Industrialised nations pursuing decarbonisation through electric vehicles, battery storage, wind turbines, and solar panels have become structurally dependent on a narrow set of critical minerals—cobalt, lithium, manganese, graphite, platinum group metals, and rare earth elements—of which Africa holds a disproportionate share. The Democratic Republic of the Congo supplies approximately 73% of global cobalt; South Africa holds over 90% of known platinum group metal reserves and 80% of manganese reserves; Zimbabwe, Namibia, Ghana, and the DRC contain substantial lithium deposits; and Tanzania and Madagascar are emerging graphite producers. Yet Africa captures a negligible fraction of the value generated by these minerals, reproducing the extractive, low-value-capture patterns that characterised the petroleum era.

This paper proposes an “Asymmetric Dependence” framework, arguing that Africa possesses a narrow but historically unique window of strategic leverage arising from the industrialised world’s dependence on African mineral supplies to achieve its own climate targets. The framework develops a governance architecture comprising four pillars: (i) export discipline mechanisms (export levies, quotas, and coordinated supply management) that internalise the strategic value of mineral endowments, (ii) beneficiation and downstream industrialisation mandates that maximise domestic value addition, (iii) strategic stockpiling and commodity exchange development that enhance market power and price stability, and (iv) South–South coalition-building—particularly through an African Critical Minerals Alliance—that amplifies collective bargaining power. Drawing on case studies from the DRC, Zimbabwe, Namibia, South Africa, Tanzania, Morocco, Madagascar, and Ghana, the paper evaluates the conditions under which African mineral states can convert geological advantage into durable developmental gains before the leverage window closes through substitution, recycling, and synthetic alternatives. The paper concludes that Africa’s critical minerals represent the continent’s most significant geoeconomic asset of the twenty-first century, but that realising their developmental potential requires a fundamental departure from the governance models that squandered the petroleum dividend.

title: Tapping the Unbanked Smallholders via Agricultural Value Chain Financing
affiliations: Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU), , University of Connecticut - Department of Operations & Information Management and Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU)

detail.title: Tapping the Unbanked Smallholders via Agricultural Value Chain Financing
detail.abstract:
Problem Definition: Smallholder farmers' limited collateral often precludes bank lending, pushing buyers to finance production directly. While buyer direct financing (BDF) relaxes credit constraints, it creates incentive misalignment: buyers exploit farmers through high interest rates in weak markets or induce overproduction through zero interest rates in strong markets. An emerging alternative is agricultural value chain financing (VCF), in which buyers and external stakeholders jointly sponsor a financing vehicle that incorporates farmer welfare into its objective function. Yet when and why VCF outperforms BDF remains unclear, particularly across varying market conditions and capital cost structures.

Methodology/Results: We develop a game-theoretic model comparing bank financing, BDF, and VCF under yield uncertainty. The model endogenizes production, wholesale pricing, and lending rates, isolating how governance of the financing vehicle reshapes operational and financial incentives. We find that VCF fundamentally alters the supply chain by decoupling lending decisions from the buyer's unilateral control. This governance innovation curbs buyer exploitation in weak markets and tempers overproduction in strong markets when the buyer's capital cost is high or downstream demand is weak. Counterintuitively, when the buyer's capital cost is low and markets are moderate, VCF intensifies double marginalization, reducing profits for both buyer and farmer. We characterize financing preference conflicts across different regimes and show that VCF may benefit the buyer at the farmer's expense, contrary to its welfare-oriented design. Nevertheless, VCF can raise aggregate supply chain efficiency even when lacking individual appeal.

Managerial Implications: The value of VCF hinges on governance structure rather than liquidity provision alone. Our results highlight VCF as a conditional governance innovation whose benefits depend on the interplay between capital constraints and market conditions. In regions with financing preference conflicts, government interventions such as interest rate caps or capital subsidies can align individual incentives with supply chain efficiency gains.

detail.abstract: Objectives: The purpose of this research is to analyse the challenges faced by English as a Foreign Language students in applying APA-style citation and referencing, as well as in summarising and paraphrasing. Using assessment data drawn from the institutional course learning outcomes (CLOs) dashboard, the study evaluates the extent to which these academic writing skills have been mastered and, in turn, determines the efficacy of current teaching strategies. Methods: Data from 60 ENG101 students at the Modern College of Business and Science in Muscat, Oman, were analysed quantitatively using a standardised assessment rubic to assess source-integration skills. Institutional CLOs' dashboard figures were also reviewed to validate rubric scores, and to identify citation and paraphrasing trends. Results: Although participants demonstrated stronger summarising and paraphrasing skills (78% and 80%, CLO 5), they struggled with citation and referencing (67% and 65%, CLO 4), with errors in accuracy, integration, and formatting. These weaknesses compromise research credibility and highlight the urgent need for targeted instructional strategies. Conclusion: Students showed stronger summarising and paraphrasing skills, but weaker citation and referencing performance. These findings underscore the need for integrated pedagogy and adaptive feedback tools. Future research should also examine broader contexts and citation styles. Contribution: The study contributes to academic writing pedagogy by identifying English as a Foreign Language students' challenges with source-integration skills, including citation, referencing, summarising, and paraphrasing, and by proposing targeted instructional strategies that foster ethical source use, strengthen academic integrity, and prepare learners for advanced research.

detail.abstract: The EU Commission's Call for Evidence on its Communication on Better Regulation extends beyond a technical consultation on how the Commission prepares its legislative proposals. It indicates the Commission's intention to institutionalise the expedited methods used to prepare the 2025 omnibus packages, turning ad hoc departures from Better Regulation into standard practice. These packages combined substantial policy reforms across sustainability, environmental protection, food safety, and digital rights while bypassing standard procedural safeguards, such as public consultation and impact assessment, thus testing the constitutional limits of EU lawmaking. The European Ombudsman's November 2025 finding of maladministration, citing insufficient justification for claimed urgency, inadequate consultation, and failure to document necessary climate assessments, should encourage reflection rather than solidify these departures. The adoption of streamlined procedures exposes a fundamental tension at the core of contemporary EU governance. On the one hand, there is the need for responsive, efficient policymaking in the “volatile geopolitical environment” outlined in this Call for Evidence. On the other side is the commitment to evidence-based, participatory, and proportionate lawmaking, which forms the procedural element of the rule of law under Article 2 TEU. This submission rejects the idea that these imperatives are opposed. The procedural safeguards integrated into Better Regulation exist not as barriers to good governance but as essential conditions for it. Evidence-based assessments ensure that regulatory decisions are grounded in facts. Stakeholder consultation enriches the decision-making evidence base. Fundamental rights screening guarantees that constitutional values are preserved and not sacrificed to political expediency. Far from hindering effective governance, these procedures support it, making legislation more likely to meet its aims, less prone to unintended consequences, and more legitimate in the eyes of those affected. Legislation passed without sufficient evidentiary support risks being ineffective, illegitimate, and potentially invalid under EU law. These procedural standards mirror those the EU enforces externally under Article 7 TEU and the Conditionality Regulation, deriving from the same constitutional sources. The effectiveness and legitimacy of external rule-of-law enforcement depend on demonstrating that procedural requirements, adequate consultation, evidence-based decision-making, and transparent legislative processes operate as binding constitutional obligations for all EU actors. Codifying Better Regulation safeguards would serve dual constitutional purposes: ensuring EU institutional compliance with Treaty obligations and strengthening the normative framework for external rule-of-law conditionality. The solution is not to abandon procedural safeguards but to codify them. The Better Regulation framework should establish objective, legally binding criteria for when expedited procedures, such as limiting consultation or omitting impact assessments, are constitutionally permissible. The Interinstitutional Agreement already requires “objective justifications based on substantive link” for bundled delegated acts. Omnibus legislation requires analogous discipline: substantive connection between measures, heightened procedural safeguards, and disaggregation when technical simplifications are bundled with policy reversals. The constitutional imperative is clear: the Commission cannot enforce rule-of-law standards against Member States while bypassing the procedural safeguards that operationalise these principles in its own lawmaking.

title: Optimal Policies for Dynamic Pricing and Inventory Control with Nonparametric Censored Demands
affiliations: University of Illinois at Chicago - College of Business Administration, University of Texas at Dallas and Tsinghua University - Yau Mathematical Sciences Center

detail.title: Optimal Policies for Dynamic Pricing and Inventory Control with Nonparametric Censored Demands
detail.abstract:
We study the fundamental model in joint pricing and inventory replenishment control under the learning-while-doing framework, with T consecutive review periods and the firm not knowing the demand curve a priori. At the beginning of each period, the retailer makes both a price decision and an inventory order-up-to level decision, and collects revenues from consumers' realized demands while suffering costs from either holding unsold inventory items, or lost sales from unsatisfied customer demands. We make the following contributions to this fundamental problem as follows:

1. We propose a novel inversion method based on empirical measures to consistently estimate the difference of the instantaneous reward functions at two prices, directly tackling the fundamental challenge brought by censored demands, without raising the order-up-to levels to unnaturally high levels to collect more demand information. Based on this technical innovation, we design bisection and trisection search methods that attain an O(T^{1/2}) regret, assuming the reward function is concave and only twice continuously differentiable.

2. In the more general case of non-concave reward functions, we design an active tournament elimination method that attains O(T^{3/5}) regret, based also on the technical innovation of consistent estimates of reward differences at two prices.

3. We complement the O(T^{3/5}) regret upper bound with a matching \Omega(T^{3/5}) regret lower bound. The lower bound is established by a novel information-theoretical argument based on generalized squared Hellinger distance, which is significantly different from conventional arguments that are based on Kullback-Leibler divergence. This lower bound shows that no learning-while-doing algorithm could achieve O(T^{1/2}) regret without assuming the reward function is concave, even if the sales revenue as a function of demand rate or price is concave.

Both the upper bound technique based on the "difference estimator" and the lower bound technique based on generalized Hellinger distance are new in the literature, and can be potentially applied to solve other inventory or censored demand type problems that involve learning.

title: Tailored Base-Surge Policies in Dual-Sourcing Inventory Systems with Demand Learning
affiliations: University of Illinois at Chicago - College of Business Administration and

detail.title: Tailored Base-Surge Policies in Dual-Sourcing Inventory Systems with Demand Learning
detail.abstract: We consider a periodic-review dual-sourcing inventory system, in which the expedited supplier is faster and more costly, while the regular supplier is slower and cheaper. Under full demand distributional information, it is well-known that the optimal policy is extremely complex but the celebrated Tailored Base-Surge (TBS) policy performs near optimally. Under such a policy, a constant order is placed at the regular source in each period, while the order placed at the expedited source follows a simple order-up-to rule. In this paper, we assume that the firm does not know the demand distribution a priori, and makes adaptive inventory ordering decisions in each period based only on the past sales (a.k.a. censored demand) data. The standard performance measure is regret, which is the cost difference between a feasible learning algorithm and the clairvoyant (full-information) benchmark. When the benchmark is chosen to be the (full-information) best Tailored Base-Surge policy, we develop the first nonparametric learning algorithm that admits a regret bound of O(√T(logT)3loglogT), which is provably tight up to a logarithmic factor. Leveraging the structure of this problem, our approach combines the power of bisection search and stochastic gradient descent and also involves a delicate high probability coupling argument between our and the clairvoyant optimal system dynamics.

detail.abstract: These remarks were prepared and delivered in October 2025 at a conference focusing on economic sanctions and other challenges to international economic ordering. I chose to focus my remarks on the Trump administration's recent use of economic sanction-type actions against enemies inside the United States. The remarks used the then-current controversy over the White House's Compact for Higher Education. The Compact has since gone down, thankfully, as a major policy failure of Trump's first year, though there are recent reports that the administration is seeking to revise and re-tool these efforts. 1 But I think what I say here about the Compact has broader significance to the tactics of the Executive Branch, particularly but not exclusively under Trump, and thus remains relevant. The arguments developed here, I submit, offer important insights into what is happening today from Minneapolis to Caracas. Following the other authors credited in the text, I encourage scholars to focus more deeply on the way that the administration is using its control over financial nodes to institute new legal forms outside of democratic control.

title: Work from Home and Fertility
affiliations: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, ITAM - Business School, Stanford University - Department of Economics, Stanford University, University of Chicago, Ifo Institute and Princeton University - Princeton University

detail.title: Work from Home and Fertility
detail.abstract: We investigate how fertility relates to work from home (WFH) in the post-pandemic era, drawing on original data from our Global Survey of Working Arrangements and U.S. Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes. Realized fertility from 2023 to early 2025 and future planned fertility are higher among adults who WFH at least one day a week and, for couples, higher yet when both partners do so. Estimated lifetime fertility is greater by 0.32 children per woman when both partners WFH one or more days per week as compared to the case where neither does. The implications for national fertility rates differ across countries due mainly to large differences in WFH rates. In a complementary analysis using other U.S. data, one-year fertility rates in the 2023-2025 period rise with WFH opportunities in one's own occupation and, for couples, in the partner's occupation. title: Model Selection in Panel Data Models: A Generalization of the Vuong Test
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Department of Economics, New York University (NYU) and New York University (NYU)

detail.title: Model Selection in Panel Data Models: A Generalization of the Vuong Test
detail.abstract: This paper generalizes the classical Vuong (1989) test to panel data models by employing modified profile likelihoods and the Kullback-Leibler information criterion. Unlike the standard likelihood function, the profile likelihood lacks certain regular properties, making modification necessary. We adopt a generalized panel data framework that incorporates group fixed effects for time and individual pairs, rather than traditional individual fixed effects. Applications of our approach include linear models with non-nested specifications of individual-time effects.

title: The Implications of TRIPs' Criminal Provisions on Copyright Exception for Education in Ethiopia: A Critical Approach from Human Rights Perspective

detail.title: The Implications of TRIPs' Criminal Provisions on Copyright Exception for Education in Ethiopia: A Critical Approach from Human Rights Perspective
detail.abstract: The criminal enforcement of intellectual property is controversial. In particular, the criminal enforcement of copyright has serious legal repercussions for vital public interests such as education. For instance, lack of sufficient access to learning materials is a significant impediment against the realisation of quality tertiary education in Ethiopia. An expansive copyright protection is one of several restrictive factors. Given its restrictive approach, the criminal measures under the Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs) might encroach upon fundamental human rights. Taking a critical perspective through a human rights lens, this article thus seeks to examine the future implications of TRIPs’ criminal provisions for tertiary education in Ethiopia. If not implemented with regard to Ethiopia's local context and development needs, it is argued that the domestic implementation of optional TRIPs’ criminal provisions will reinforce the existing restrictive copyright system at the expense of the realisation of tertiary education.

title: YouTubers and Stock Returns
affiliations: XLRI – Xavier School of Management and

detail.title: YouTubers and Stock Returns
detail.abstract: We use a Large Language Model (Gemini) to extract stock recommendations from YouTubers' videos across nine countries and test whether these recommendations carry predictive power for future stock returns. Our analysis reveals that the average sentiment score derived from YouTube videos predicts one-monthahead returns, but not returns at longer horizons. We find no evidence that videos with higher views have greater information content for future returns, nor that the predictability is affected by stock market capitalization. These results suggest that, on average, stock signals from social media platforms like YouTube contain information relevant for short-term price movements, but are unlikely to generate sustained medium-term profits for investors. Our findings contribute to the emerging literature on the role of financial influencers in capital markets and highlight the importance of understanding the informational value-and limitations-of social media-based financial advice.

title: The Disputed Constitutionality of the Precedential Practice of the Federal Supreme Court and Its Implications for Oromia Family Law: The Case of Bigamous Marriage in Ethiopia

detail.title: The Disputed Constitutionality of the Precedential Practice of the Federal Supreme Court and Its Implications for Oromia Family Law: The Case of Bigamous Marriage in Ethiopia
detail.abstract: The practice of cassation over cassation and its consequent rule of precedent have resulted in a legal quagmire. The impact is evident in the pecuniary disposition of a bigamous marriage with far-reaching legal ramifications for a valid marriage in Ethiopia. In fact, the pecuniary consequences of a bigamous marriage have remained a perplexing challenge in Ethiopia due to, inter alia, the debatable precedential practice of the Federal Supreme Court. Given the constitutionally guaranteed regional autonomy of the regional states to regulate family matters in Ethiopia, the practice has constitutional implications for the application of the Oromia Family Code. This article argues that the federal doctrine of precedent and its enabling legislation not only lack a concrete constitutional basis, but also encroach upon the constitutional autonomy of regional states and the constitutional rights of legitimate spouses. Exploring the constitutional dimensions of the practice and its legal ramifications, the article suggests possible options to change the practice at a regional level.

title: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Robust Cognition in Neural Networks
affiliations: Imperial College London - Department of Mathematics

detail.title: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Robust Cognition in Neural Networks
detail.abstract: We propose a game-theoretic framework for modeling cognition as a problem of robust coordination in neural networks. Building on a geometric theory of payoff spaces and incentive robustness, we model neurons or small neural assemblies as strategic agents whose spiking decisions are governed by context-dependent payoff tensors. Cognitive states correspond to Nash equilibria of multi-agent coordination games, while qualitative shifts in cognition arise from small perturbations that move the system across payoff-space boundaries where best-response correspondences change discontinuously. Robust cognition is characterized geometrically as distance from indifference manifolds in payoff space. The framework provides a unified account of neural assemblies, attentional stability, neuromodulation, and cognitive control, and connects naturally to minimax and robust control formulations of perception under uncertainty.

title: The Liquidation of Pecuniary Effects of Bigamous Marriage in Ethiopia: A Critical Review of the Precedents of the Federal Supreme Court and Rule of Equity under the Oromia Regional Family Code

detail.title: The Liquidation of Pecuniary Effects of Bigamous Marriage in Ethiopia: A Critical Review of the Precedents of the Federal Supreme Court and Rule of Equity under the Oromia Regional Family Code
detail.abstract: In Ethiopia, the effects of the liquidation of assets on the dissolution of bigamous marriages are posing more of a threat to the exclusivity of a valid marriage than bigamy itself. However, the Oromia Family Code has conceived a device that curbs the practice, namely a rule of equity to govern the liquidation process. Nevertheless, the rule is seemingly neglected in judicial practice. This article examines the application of the rule in the liquidation of the pecuniary effects of a bigamous marriage. To this end, the article critically analyses the interplay between the rule of equity under the Oromia Family Code and the precedents of the Federal Supreme Court in the liquidation. It concludes that the inconsistent precedential practice of the Federal Supreme Court has marginalized the application of the rule of equity under the Code. Thus, the existing precedents should be revisited in future cases to take into account the rule of equity for cases originating from the region. In so doing, the-much-neglected and disowned rule of equity must be revisited to reshape the status quo.

It is the actual disclosure language of Circle Internet Group, Inc. in their prospectus that is the focus of the article.

title: Causal Dempster-Shafer Extension for Situational State Estimation Using Belief Evolution and Ballparking
affiliations: Senslytics Corporation

detail.title: Causal Dempster-Shafer Extension for Situational State Estimation Using Belief Evolution and Ballparking
detail.abstract: Process engineering systems often operate under deep uncertainty, delayed or asynchronous evidence arrival, and heterogeneous sensing modalities. Classical probabilistic methods struggle to represent incomplete information and rare occurrences, while real-time industrial decision processes frequently depend on coarse-grained ballparking to avoid false precision and maintain operational tempo. This paper addresses the long-standing gap between evidence accumulation, real-world causal dynamics, and industry ballparking practice by introducing a principled framework for belief evolution under uncertainty. Many of the mechanisms formalized here have already been implemented in proprietary CausX AI technology, and applications built on this causal-epistemic foundation have been successfully piloted across multiple industrial domains over the past several years, as documented in prior publications and patented inventions. However, a rigorous theoretical foundation for these ideas has not previously existed. The proposed framework integrates Situational Awareness, Dempster Shafer Theory, and a formalized Ballparking Operator to support robust reasoning in time-delayed, scienti cally grounded, causation-rich environments. The mathematical formulation demonstrates how ballparking can be embedded within DST as a bounded-rationality operator that accelerates decision-making without compromising epistemic rigor. It further formalizes how beliefs evolve over time when observations, ignorance, and causal structure jointly shape the inference process. The resulting methods are designed explicitly for industrial problem solving. This formulation extends Dempster Shafer Theory and causal models toward more dependable interpretation of rare events, principled con ict resolution, and stable belief maturation in high-uncertainty environments.Applications span geological, chemical, and biological process-engineering domains, including oil and gas operations, pipeline integrity management, grain preservation, drug discovery, and complex medical treatments. This work initiates the development of a comprehensive theoretical foundation for CausX AI, establishing the basis for a progressively more robust, uni ed, and scalable paradigm for industrial analytics and decision support across diverse domains.

title: Stock Markets and Economic Growth: Global and Country-Group Evidence Using Bayesian Panel Vector Autoregression Models

detail.title: Stock Markets and Economic Growth: Global and Country-Group Evidence Using Bayesian Panel Vector Autoregression Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I am the sole author of this research. I declare that I have no financial or personal relationships with other people or organizations that could have influenced my study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a theoretical and empirical analysis in economics and does not involve human participants or animal subjects. Therefore, ethical approval was not required for this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was conducted independently using my own resources.

publicationDetails.detailsText: The B.E. Journal of Macroeconomics, December 2025

detail.abstract: The relationship between stock market development and economic growth remains the subject of considerable debate, with growing empirical evidence yielding ambiguous results. This study challenges the conventional narrative of a positive and universal link between the stock market and economic growth by addressing a key limitation in the literature: the implicit assumption of homogeneity in multi-country analyses. To this end, I employ a Bayesian Vector Autoregressive (BVAR) framework estimated individually for a global panel of 93 economies from 1996 to 2024, allowing for the explicit modeling of idiosyncratic structural dynamics. The findings do not reveal a systematic or statistically significant effect of stock market shocks on economic growth. The dominant result is immense heterogeneity, where the null average effect masks a wide dispersion of positive, negative, and neutral responses at the country level. Moreover, the forecast error variance decomposition consistently shows that external factors, particularly shocks to the real exchange rate, are the main drivers of economic growth variability. The study concludes that the finance-growth nexus is not universal, but is heterogeneous and highly contingent upon the idiosyncratic characteristics of each country.

title: Equilibrium Compliance under Transitory Visibility

detail.title: Equilibrium Compliance under Transitory Visibility
detail.abstract: I study how compliance responds dynamically to temporary, highly visible policy interventions. I develop a coordination framework in which visibility raises contemporaneous compliance by activating marginal adopters, while postintervention persistence depends on belief updating within local social networks. As visibility fades, compliance attenuates at a rate governed by social cohesion. I test the framework using a randomised field experiment in dense urban neighbourhoods. Compliance rises sharply during the intervention but decays afterward, with significantly slower decay in more cohesive communities. Welfare counterfactuals show that short, salient interventions can generate substantial gains when targeted to cohesive networks.

title: Explanation of the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) Framework in Strategic Performance Management

detail.title: Explanation of the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) Framework in Strategic Performance Management
detail.abstract: One of the most persistent problems in management theory and practice is the gap between strategic intent and day-today execution. Businesses need to develop new performance measurement systems to help solve complex issues. One such measurement system is objectives and key results (OKRs), which has been adopted by Google with great success (Rompho, 2024). Organizations often articulate compelling visions yet struggle to convert them into coordinated action across teams and individuals. The OKR framework, short for Objectives and Key Results, emerged as a response to this challenge by offering a structured yet flexible approach to goal setting. At a doctoral level, OKRs should be understood not merely as a performance management tool but as a socio-cognitive system that links ambition, measurement, and learning within organizations. Without a clear objective, operations between departments would be disordered and inconsistent. Therefore, top management teams should first set objectives, and then distribute responsibilities down to the lower-tier management levels, where lower-tier management objectives must be consistent with those set by upper-level management (Rompho, 2024). OKRs have mainly been examined from a managerial perspective in practitioner oriented outlets, but rarely from an academic perspective. In response, OKRs need further investigation that is scientifically sound in order to address the current research gap that exists regarding OKRs as a tool that middle managers can use to enhance the strategy implementation process (Wowerath, 2026). Many highly successful organizations have adopted OKRs such as Intuit, the Gates Foundation, Adobe and Intel. After Intel implemented OKRs, Google adopted the idea, achieved great success, and expanded this idea globally. However, this concept is still being investigated and currently, no study has investigated the use of OKRs within organizations (Rompho, 2024).

title: The Effect of Policies that Tackle the Preference for Sons: Evidence from India

detail.title: The Effect of Policies that Tackle the Preference for Sons: Evidence from India
detail.abstract: I assess the effect of an Indian government reform that aims to improve the ratio of female to male births. In contrast to monetary incentives, this ongoing program leverages community engagement and media campaigns to shift social norms and enhance the perceived value of daughters. Exploiting the phased rollout of the program across administrative units, I find that early-implementing units experienced a 1.5 percentage point increase in the probability of a female birth, equivalent to approximately 15 additional female births per 1,000 births over a five-year period. For second and higherorder births, where preference for sons is more pronounced, the estimated effect is larger at 2.1 percentage points. These results underscore the potential for non-financial, norm-based policy interventions to complement financial incentives in improving the gender balance at birth.

title: Drug Policy, Harm Reduction, and Christian Institutional Justice: A Constrained Public-Economics Approach
affiliations: Liberty University

detail.title: Drug Policy, Harm Reduction, and Christian Institutional Justice: A Constrained Public-Economics Approach
detail.abstract: This article develops a public-economics framework for evaluating drug policy in which Christian conceptions of justice operate as binding institutional constraints rather than as welfare weights. Standard economic analyses of drug prohibition typically treat incarceration, collateral sanctions, and enforcement disparities as costs to be balanced against reductions in drug consumption or crime. This approach obscures whether such outcomes are morally admissible at all. Drawing on Christian social thought, the paper identifies three justice constraints-limits on coercive captivity, distributional injustice, and permanent exclusion-and incorporates them into a constrained optimization framework. Within this framework, conventional prohibitionist drug regimes become normatively inadmissible, not merely inefficient, because their institutional logic predictably violates these constraints. By contrast, harm-reduction and health-oriented regimes remain feasible and perform comparatively well on conventional outcome measures such as mortality, public health, and fiscal cost. The analysis demonstrates how Christian ethics can discipline economic reasoning without displacing it and argues that harm reduction represents the most defensible institutional response to drug use once justice-based limits on coercion are taken seriously.

title: Markov-Switching Multifractal Models for High-Frequency Trade Counts
affiliations: and Vrije Universiteit (VU) Amsterdam

detail.title: Markov-Switching Multifractal Models for High-Frequency Trade Counts
detail.abstract: This study extends the Markov-switching multifractal Poisson model for counts by incorporating zero inflation and adopting a generalized Poisson distribution. The zero-inflation component enables explicitly setting the probability of zeros, while the more general distribution provides control over the degree of conditional overdispersion (i.e., given the intensity) and a greater degree of flexibility overall. The new models are applied to high-frequency trade count data for ten NYSE-listed stocks. The results suggest that the generalized Poisson distribution can account for part of the volatility generated by the intensity process in the basic model. The extensions are found to substantially improve goodness of fit, with additional gains in forecasting.

title: Stereotypes in the Machine: Gender and Racial Bias in LLM-Generated Financial Advice
affiliations: Lingnan University and Lingnan University

detail.title: Stereotypes in the Machine: Gender and Racial Bias in LLM-Generated Financial Advice
detail.abstract: We conduct a large-scale controlled experiment of large language models (LLMs) acting as financial advisors. We find that LLMs systematically recommend lower equity allocations to female and Asian clients compared to otherwise identical White males. This bias persists and even intensifies for financially sophisticated investors, rejecting rational statistical discrimination in favor of stereotyping. While higher model intelligence mitigates these biases, standard safety alignment and explicit debiasing prompts prove ineffective. Our results suggest that without advanced reasoning capabilities, AI advisors risk institutionalizing wealth disparities by projecting demographic stereotypes onto investment decisions.

title: Calendar Spreads as Autonomous Liquidity Pools in Bond Futures Markets
affiliations: University of Portsmouth and

detail.title: Calendar Spreads as Autonomous Liquidity Pools in Bond Futures Markets
detail.abstract: This paper examines rollover activity in European government bond futures using a triangular market structure linking the nearest contract, the second-nearest contract, and their calendar spread. Using ultra-high-frequency limit order book data from EUREX, comprising over 127 million updates across nine sovereign bond futures and ten depth levels, we analyse market behaviour during the ten trading days preceding contract expiry. We document a systematic and predictable reallocation of liquidity within this triangle as expiry approaches. While activity migrates from the expiring contract to the next contract, the calendar spread emerges as an autonomous liquidity pool rather than a residual combination of its outright legs. During the peak rollover window, spreads exhibit tighter bid-ask spreads, more concentrated top-of-book liquidity, and heightened trading intensity than either outright contract. Crosscountry and maturity differences reflect variation in sovereign risk, investor composition, and duration exposure.

title: Capital Gains Awareness amongst Investors & Individual

detail.title: Capital Gains Awareness amongst Investors & Individual
